I. GENERAL
Gender-based violence and violence against children is a social phenomenon that has existed since ancient times and has become increasingly prevalent recently. In fact, gender-based violence and violence against children continues to increase, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are becoming increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, trafficking of women and children, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, exploitation of migrant workers, and neglect, will apparently continue to be encountered in daily life, both in the domestic sphere (household) and public sphere.
The causal factors of gender-based violence and violence against children are very complex and interrelated with one another. These factors include, among others, legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the concept that women and children are family property (assets), media that lack support in reporting on violence against women and children, public services that are not yet optimal, customs that sometimes legalize violence, poverty issues, erroneous interpretations of religious teachings, all of which are wrapped in a patriarchal culture.
The handling of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children occurring in Ogan Komering Ulu Regency, in accordance with the provisions of Article 13 of Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, states that Regional Governments are obligated to establish and develop a system and mechanism of cooperation for handling violence. Furthermore, based on the provisions of Article 26 paragraph (1) letter b of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government, it states that the Deputy Regional Head has the duty to assist the Regional Head in coordinating the activities of vertical agencies in the region, following up on reports and/or findings from supervisory apparatus oversight, implementing women's and youth empowerment, as well as endeavoring to develop and preserve socio-cultural life and the environment. Therefore, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children.

CHAPTER VII
PREVENTION OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE
Article 24
(1) To prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children, the Regional Government conducts socialization, empowerment, and awareness-raising to families, parents, and the community by providing information, guidance and/or outreach.
(2) In addition to empowerment and awareness-raising as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government undertakes efforts as follows:
a. increasing the quantity and quality of education both formal and non-formal and informal;
b. opening employment opportunities for women;
c. building community participation and concern towards the prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence; and
d. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children.

Article 7
(1) Integrated services as referred to in Article 6 letter a shall be established by the Regional Government in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) The establishment of integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of members from regional government elements, non-governmental institutions, health service institutions, law enforcement officers, professional workers, volunteer companions, social workers, religious leaders, safe houses (shelters), and social rehabilitation centers.

Article 21
(1) In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the regional government may cooperate with the Government, other Regional Governments.
(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government includes consultation, coordination and reporting.
(3) Cooperation between the Regional Government and other Regional Governments includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration and development of integrated service systems.

Article 16
(1) KPK2BGA as referred to in Article 6 letter b, shall be established by the Regional Government in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) The establishment of KPK2BGA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of members from elements of SKPD responsible for Health affairs, SKPD responsible for Social and Labor affairs, Police, community leaders, religious leaders, non-governmental organization activists, academics, and practitioners.

CHAPTER VIII

Article 25
(1) Control, guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be carried out by the Regent, the execution of which shall be carried out by the Vice Regent.
(2) The implementation of control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall, on a day-to-day basis, be carried out by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.
Letter b What is meant by "the best interests of the victim" is that in all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, the community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.
Letter c What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.
What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, aligned and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in community, national and state life.
Letter d What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court determination.
Letter e What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not die during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions.
Letter f What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to be creative and to engage in recreation.
What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.
Letter g What is meant by "respect for the child's opinion" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.
Letter h What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among integrated service providers and KPK2BGA.
Letter i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.
Letter j What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.
Letter k What is meant by "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, whether physically, psychologically, socially or economically.
Letter l What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.
Letter m What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.
